- What retention windows do you offer for audit logs vs access logs by default in the hosted product?
- If we request data deletion (e.g., account closure or a DSAR), how long until exported snapshots and internal backups are purged?

Subject: Re: Questions on log export & deletion windows

Hi all — providing the security/compliance answers below. Ive kept the responses concise; happy to expand in a call or provide copies of the export schema.

1) Export windows and methods- Ad-hoc exports: Console and the Logs Export API allow arbitrary day-range selection up to the last 365 days for hosted accounts by default.
- Scheduled exports: We support daily or weekly scheduled exports to an S3-compatible destination or Google Cloud Storage. Schedule cadence: daily, weekly. Monthly snapshots are supported via custom config (managed via Support/Professional Services).
- Export formats: CSV and NDJSON (structured), plus pre-signed encrypted bundles for bulk transfers.

2) Retention defaults- Audit logs (admin actions, role changes, RBAC events): default retention 2 years for hosted by standard plan; Dedicated/Private customers can set custom retention via policy.
- Access logs (request traces, token usage, IPs): default retention 90 days for hosted; 1 year available on request or as part of our Optimize/Enterprise tiers.

3) Deletion & DSARs/account offboarding- Immediate: when a deletion request is submitted, we delete indexed records and stop further retention processing within 48 hours (visible in Console as "Deletion in progress").- Backups & exported snapshots: exported files that were pushed to a customer-managed destination remain under customer's control and are not deleted by Redwood. For exports stored in Redwood-managed export buckets (rare, by exception), Redwood retains copies for up to 30 days post-export and then purges them, unless a longer retention was agreed contractually.
- Final purge: internal immutable backups (for disaster recovery) are rotated on a 90-day cycle; data subject to deletion requests is marked and excluded from restores; full physical purge from all internal backups completes within 120 days of the approved deletion request unless legal hold is applied.

4) Audit trail & proof of deletion- We provide an audit record (exportable) that shows the deletion request, operator, and timestamp; for DSARs we can produce a certificate of deletion (signed metadata) on request.

5) Constraints & notes- For customers operating in-region with Private deployments, retention windows are enforced by the customer's policy and can differ.
- Exporting very large windows (>180 days of high-cardinality request logs) is rate-limited and may be chunked; we provide pre-signed manifests to assemble the complete export.

Action items: Hannah, can you produce a short one-page summary tailored to Acme Health with the specific defaults and contract exceptions we discussed? Neha, Ill attach the log policy PDF and an export sample to this thread.

-Marissa Cole
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Jay — attaching the one-pager with the exact retention table we recommend for Health customers and a short FAQ for procurement. Summary highlights in-line:

- Default hosted retention: Audit logs = 24 months; Access logs = 90 days.
- Optional extensions: Access logs can be extended to 12 months via Enterprise add-on; Audit logs configurable to indefinite for Dedicated/Private.
- Deletion timeline: Deletion requests are acted on within 48 hours; final purge from internal backups completes within 120 days unless legal hold.
- Export notes: Exports can be scheduled daily/weekly; ad-hoc exports support arbitrary date ranges up to the last 365 days (we can increase with a contract clause).

Please review the attached PDF and let me know if you want us to populate the template you sent with sample values — we can return it by Monday.
